title: Capture a separate PCSX2 log for a launch test
summary: Use `-logfile` to direct one PCSX2 launch’s log to a dedicated file, then verify the file before sharing diagnostics.
heroAlt: Rear right view of a slim PlayStation 2 console showing its ports.
author: EmuCore - Hub
searchKeywords: write a separate pcsx2 log for a command line launch test
Capture a separate PCSX2 log for a launch test

blocks.text: PCSX2 documents `-logfile <path>` as writing the application log to a chosen path instead of the usual `emulog.txt`. A dedicated file makes it easier to compare one launch attempt without mixing older output. Logs can contain local paths or diagnostic details, so inspect and redact private information before sending a copy to anyone.

Use a directory where your account can create files and choose a new filename, not an existing log that matters. Keep the normal PCSX2 shortcut unchanged. Write down the exact action you will test and avoid changing unrelated graphics, controller, or BIOS settings during the capture.

items: 1. Create or choose a writable diagnostics folder and decide on a unique log filename.
2. Copy your usual PCSX2 shortcut or command line.
3. Add `-logfile` followed by the full log path before the game image argument.
4. Launch PCSX2 and reproduce the single issue once; stop after the failure or checkpoint you are investigating.
5. Close PCSX2 normally so buffered log data is flushed.
6. Open the new file, confirm it has recent content, and search for the timestamp or error matching the test.

blocks.text: The capture passes when a new or updated file appears at the chosen path and contains entries from the test you just ran. Check its modification time and confirm the tested title or startup stage is represented. An empty file or old timestamp means the launch did not use the intended option or could not write to that location.

items: No file appears: confirm the path exists, is writable, and follows your shell’s quoting rules.
The normal emulog changed instead: confirm the copied launch target actually includes `-logfile`.
The log stops early: close PCSX2 normally and repeat once if a crash prevented flushing.
The log contains personal paths: redact them before sharing; do not publish BIOS or game files with the log.

blocks.text: Remove `-logfile` from the copied command and return to the normal shortcut. Keep the diagnostic file only as long as needed, then delete it using your usual file-management process after confirming it is not the only record of the issue.
